title: The conductor stands his ground
body: In A.G. Gardiner's 'All about a Dog', a bus conductor stops his bus on a bitterly cold night because a lady in sealskin has brought her Pekinese dog inside. The passengers protest angrily and someone rings the bell. A policeman strolls up and looks in at the door. An avalanche of indignant protests and appeals bursts on him. "Well, he's got his rules, you know," he says. "Give your name and address." When told that the conductor has been offered this and will not take it, the policeman simply says "Oh" and takes his stand a few yards down the street, where two more constables join him. Meanwhile the little dog blinks at the lights, and the conductor walks to and fro on the pavement, like a captain on the quarterdeck in the hour of victory. A young woman descends on him angrily, but he is as immovable as the cold night and as hard as the pavement.
